reason: Test-harness repair only, no product code. Since b833782 Core's API process refuses a mutation without a client Idempotency-Key (428) and may answer with a saved-request receipt, prints its address before its API process is admitted, keeps its retained release read-only, and leaves detached runtime workers and a /tmp socket directory behind when only serve is stopped; real-core.spec.ts did none of this, so every journey on a full Core failed at its first setup mutation or in cleanup. This change adds ui/tests/fixtures/core-api.ts (byte-identical to #1067's) and core-harness.ts (a keyed request wrapper built on coreMutation, worker and socket teardown), wires real-core.spec.ts to them (keyed request contexts, an API readiness wait, teardown of workers, sockets and data, runtime-adopt for a data root seeded before the first start, three inline seed scripts that awaited an async context manager), adds two checks for the helpers and a one-profile catalogue area, real-core-harness. Selected: that area (the five owned-cleanup checks, two of them new: an inert keyed-request check and a real-Core teardown check), three journeys that exercise the wrapper against a real supervisor Core or a fixture Core and passed locally on desktop Chromium on main 3c0481c (mcp-context, chat-edit-in-place, assistant-queue-core), and the Playwright impact manifest tests, because ui/playwright-impact.json gained the area and its rule.
exclusions: Only assistant-real-desktop profiles: the change is in the Node-side harness, not in layout. No other real-Core area is selected because most still fail on main for product reasons that this change does not touch (project views of a chatless project answer 503, the execution guard rejects ORM updates of notes, storage sender tokens are refused, cold project workers start slowly); the per-journey classes are in the PR. tests/test_playwright_impact.py::test_full_manifest_covers_every_product_browser_spec_without_filters is left out: it fails identically on pristine main; the other 40 tests of that file are selected by name. No frontend or native code changed. Journeys were run locally against a production UI build with a Python 3.12 Core, the scratch host-pressure shim and a per-journey user scope; nothing was deployed.
